clue.text: Occasionally won hand with ten high

indicators.note: high here means intoxicated, so the letters before it are scrambled

explanation.surface: A card player's lucky moment: winning a hand holding the ten as the top card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' looks like a card ranking but signals the anagram; 'with' just joins WON HAND and TEN, whose ten letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning from time to time, at irregular intervals.

clue.text: Basis of short drama initially taking shape

indicators.note: short means the word for drama loses its final letter

parts.note: a play is a drama

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of taking is used

parts.note: first letter of taking
form means shape

explanation.surface: Describes how a brief play first starts to come together.
explanation.definitionFit: A platform is a foundation or base on which something, such as a policy, is built.

clue.text: Scottish writer in pub about to imbibe one

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: to imbibe is to drink in, so the word for about takes in the numeral

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about, concerning
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Scottish author is in a pub, about to have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to imbibe' reads as 'on the point of drinking', but 'about' is RE and 'to imbibe' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie, author of Peter Pan, was born in Kirriemuir, Scotland.

clue.text: Livestock finally destroy a beautiful orchid

parts.note: cattle are livestock

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of destroy is used

parts.note: last letter of destroy

explanation.surface: Farm animals end up trampling a lovely orchid.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattleya is a genus of showy tropical American orchids, prized for their large blooms.

clue.text: Unusual circle for member of the clergy

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters of circle are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An odd ring is somehow suited to a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric is a priest or other ordained person in a church.

clue.text: Songstress ultimately wrong leaving du Maurier character

indicators.note: ultimately points to the closing letter of Songstress

parts.note: last letter of Songstress

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are set out incorrectly, rearranged

explanation.surface: A female singer finally goes astray by departing a novel's cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' looks like an instruction to remove letters, but it is the fodder: S, then LEAVING rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali is the sinister hypnotist in George du Maurier's novel Trilby, who turns Trilby into a singer.

clue.text: Regular publication? University breaking record

indicators.note: breaking means the abbreviation for university splits the record word

parts.note: an annal is a record of a year's events

explanation.surface: A college breaks a record, perhaps reported in a regular magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a book or periodical published once a year, hence regularly.

clue.text: Huge amount of land in Kansas I acquired

indicators.note: in signals the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of acquiring a vast tract of land in Kansas.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent, by far the greatest landmass on Earth.

clue.text: Member of parliament in bowler

indicators.note: in signals the answer lies inside the word bowler

explanation.surface: An MP is in a bowler hat, the old City of London uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: A parliament is the collective noun for a group of owls, so a member of one is a bird, not a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective noun idiom: a gathering of these birds is called a parliament.

clue.text: Not missing any of the competitions whatever happens?

definitions.text: Not missing any of the competitions
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: present at every one of the events
second meaning: in any case, regardless

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is read literally first as attending every event, then in its usual sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in any case or regardless, while literally it describes being at every contest.

clue.text: A sailor gripping line where knot may be tied

indicators.note: gripping means the sailor phrase holds the letter for line inside it

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman holds a rope where he might tie a knot.
explanation.walkthrough: The knot is the marriage one: 'tying the knot' means getting married.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples are married at the altar, and to tie the knot is an idiom for wedding.

clue.text: A truant released large American spider

indicators.note: released means the letters are let loose and rearranged

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A schoolchild skipping class sets free a big American spider.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy spider found in the Americas.

clue.text: See cod? I see flounders!

indicators.note: flounders means struggles clumsily, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A fishy exchange: look at the cod; I see flounders too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flounders' looks like more fish but signals the anagram; 'See' is the definition, a bishop's area.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the district under a bishop's authority, which is a diocese.

clue.text: Almost heaven after tea, this French wine

indicators.note: after means the trimmed heaven follows tea

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: almost means the word for heaven stops one letter short

parts.note: bliss is heaven, perfect happiness

explanation.surface: Bliss nearly reached after a cup of tea and a glass of French white.
explanation.definitionFit: Chablis is a dry white wine from the Burgundy region of France.

clue.text: Imply skip is riveted

parts.note: to spell can mean to imply or signify, as in 'this spells trouble'
bound means to leap or skip

explanation.surface: A cryptic statement that hinting at skipping keeps something fixed in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Riveted, in the sense of having one's attention held completely, means enthralled.

clue.text: Emblem of Communism in Kremlin made cash when exploited

indicators.note: exploited means put to use or worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Soviet leaders in the Kremlin profited when they exploited workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'when' are link words; only KREMLIN MADE CASH is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossed hammer and sickle symbol stood for the union of industrial and farm workers on the Soviet flag.

clue.text: Service still very good around middle of evening

parts.note: even can mean still, as in 'even better'

indicators.note: around means very and good together surround the central letter

parts.note: so means very

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of evening

parts.note: middle letter of evening

explanation.surface: A church service, still very good around the middle of the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican service of evening prayer, also called vespers.

clue.text: Fell over below unpleasant photographer's place?

indicators.note: below means the reversed word sits under the first in this down answer

parts.note: dark can mean grim or unpleasant

indicators.note: over means the word for fell is turned backwards

parts.note: a fell is a hill or moor in northern England

explanation.surface: Someone fell over beneath something nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like a verb; it is the noun for upland moor. In a down clue, 'below' puts that piece second.
explanation.definitionFit: A darkroom is the unlit room where film photographers develop prints.

clue.text: Reminder to hang on to rice wine

parts.note: to keep is to hang on to
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: A souvenir worth treasuring: a bottle of Japanese rice wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is a small item kept as a memento of a person or occasion.

clue.text: Beginning to develop touch of nerves before climb?

indicators.note: a touch of means just a small part, the first letter of nerves

parts.note: first letter of nerves
an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A climber feels the first signs of nerves before setting out.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent describes something just coming into existence, emerging.

clue.text: Husband maybe needs support after blowing top

indicators.note: blowing top means losing the first letter, the top in a down answer

parts.note: to espouse a cause is to support it

explanation.surface: A man needs backing after losing his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' sounds like losing one's temper; here it drops the top letter of ESPOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband is one example of a married partner, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Work hard in attempt to make pot

indicators.note: in means work and hard go inside the attempt word

parts.note: a try is an attempt
op is short for opus, a work
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone works hard in an attempt to make a clay pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' suggests pottery, but sporting slang calls a cup or prize a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is sporting slang for a trophy or cup, as in 'the club's first pot in years'.

clue.text: Unfair treatment in chilly and damp Kent town

parts.note: raw weather is cold and damp
Deal is a seaside town in Kent, England

explanation.surface: Bad treatment in a cold, wet seaside town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw deal is an idiom for unfair or harsh handling.

clue.text: Bet involving northern composer

indicators.note: involving means the bet word takes in the abbreviation for northern

parts.note: a wager is a bet

explanation.surface: A wager concerning a composer from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Wagner was the German composer of the Ring cycle operas.

clue.text: Cursory survey of English river led by famous explorer

indicators.note: led by means the explorer comes first

parts.note: Captain James Cook was a famous English explorer
the Stour is the name of several rivers in England

explanation.surface: An English river trip guided by a renowned explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Cook's package tours gave the phrase; the clue swaps in Captain Cook.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cook's tour is an idiom for a rapid, superficial look around, after Thomas Cook's guided tours.

clue.text: Conservative politician describing a holiday complex

indicators.note: describing means drawing a line around, so the Conservative politician surrounds the a

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Tory politician describes a holiday resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday camp is a resort with chalets and entertainment, so camp alone names such a site.

clue.text: Blow in bursts with old zest

parts.note: to gust is to blow in sudden bursts

explanation.surface: Wind blowing in bursts with old-fashioned energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto means hearty enjoyment or enthusiasm, the same as zest.

clue.text: Scrooge, say, as represented in metaphors

indicators.note: represented means presented anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Scrooge appears as a figure in metaphors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word; the fodder is IN METAPHORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's Ebenezer Scrooge is an example of a misanthrope, a hater of humankind.

clue.text: Mostly considerate family

indicators.note: mostly means the word for considerate loses its last letter

parts.note: kind means considerate

explanation.surface: A family that is mostly thoughtful.
explanation.definitionFit: Kin means relatives, one's family collectively.
